rich_summary: This section recounts the origin of Sikhandin and the vow that will one day bring about Bhishma’s fall. After the wronged princess Amba performs severe austerities, the god Siva appears and promises that she will be the cause of Bhishma’s death, even granting that she will gain manhood in another birth and remember her former life. Filled with wrath, Amba immolates herself to fulfill that destiny. Later, King Drupada, desiring a son who will destroy Bhishma, also worships Siva. The god foretells that the child will first be female and later male. When Drupada’s queen gives birth to a daughter, the couple secretly raises her as a son and names her Sikhandin. Only a few know the truth. The child is trained as a warrior and even married as a man, setting the stage for the prophecy that will ultimately lead to Bhishma’s downfall.

highlight_spans.why: Siva appears to the ascetic Amba, establishing the divine intervention that drives the entire prophecy.
The moment Siva manifests in his true form, marking the turning point where Amba’s austerities bear fruit.
The presence of the great Rishis frames the revelation as a witnessed sacred event.
Amba’s appeal to the god reflects the emotional core of the episode—her burning desire for vengeance on Bhishma.

top_scenes.scene_text: Siva, bearing the trident and radiant with divine power, appears before the ascetic Amba surrounded by silent forest sages.
Amba, filled with wrath, steps into a blazing funeral pyre on the banks of the Yamuna while declaring Bhishma’s destruction.
In Drupada’s palace, the newborn daughter secretly proclaimed a son is ceremonially named Sikhandin while only the king and queen know the truth.
